evals.name: lint-count-gets-per-file-ceilings-in-the-required-job
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet our in-house lint rule no-raw-sql. Our linter, `python3 tools/lint.py`, has no baseline file and no autofix. `python3 tools/lint.py --rule no-raw-sql --per-file` prints one `<path> violations=<n>` line per file, 37 in total, and exits 0. CI has no ratchet yet; the required check is the `verify` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
evals.expected_output: Takes the per-file baseline path, since the fix is not mechanical and the linter has no native baseline. Measures with ratchet.py add --per-file, recording each file's measured count as its own ceiling, not one repository-wide 37, in a new .ratchets.json at the repository root, passing --file .ratchets.json on every ratchet.py call and --break-glass for the new file. Vendors ratchet.py beside it without the two generated header lines. Adds one check step inside the `verify` job that runs the vendored script with --file .ratchets.json. Writes the files uncommitted, does not merge, and routes to /source-control:pull-request.
expectations: Runs ratchet.py add with --per-file, so each file keeps its own measured ceiling rather than one total of 37
Proposes .ratchets.json at the repository root and passes --file .ratchets.json to add and check
Puts the check step inside the `verify` job, the required check
Commits, pushes and merges nothing; the Output block ends awaiting human approval

evals.name: refuses-a-duration-ceiling
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet our API test suite takes 212 seconds in CI. Freeze that as a ceiling so it never gets slower.
evals.expected_output: Declines to ratchet a wall-clock duration: it moves with runner load, so the ceiling would fail at random and invite someone to raise it. Names a count that moves only with the code (number of tests, HTTP calls, database queries per run) as the thing to ratchet instead, or says there is nothing to ratchet until such a counter exists. Runs no ratchet.py add on the duration.
expectations: Does not record a ceiling on 212 seconds or any duration
States that a duration ceiling fails with host load rather than with the code
Names a counter to ratchet instead, or says one must exist first

evals.name: zero-count-lands-the-rule
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the ruff rule B006 (mutable default arguments). `ruff check --select B006 --statistics` reports 0 violations today.
evals.expected_output: Lands the rule: turns B006 on in the ruff configuration so the build fails on the first violation, and writes no ceilings entry and no CI ratchet step, because a zero count needs no ceiling. Reports that the rule landed and that no ceiling was recorded.
expectations: Turns the rule on in the linter configuration so a violation fails the build
Writes no ceilings file entry and runs no ratchet.py add
Reports that the rule landed with no ceiling

evals.name: joins-the-existing-performance-ceilings-file
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the count of `# type: ignore` comments; `python3 tools/count_ignores.py` prints ignores=9. CI already runs `python3 .performance/ratchet.py check` in the required `tests` job.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing check call, sees no --file, and so adds the counter to .performance/ratchets.json, the script's default, using the repository's vendored .performance/ratchet.py. Proposes no .ratchets.json and no second CI step, since the existing step already checks that file. Records a ceiling of 9.
expectations: Adds the counter to .performance/ratchets.json
Does not propose .ratchets.json or a second ceilings file
Adds no new CI step, because the existing check covers the file
Records a ceiling of 9

evals.name: refuses-to-merge-the-tighten-pr
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet set up the weekly job that lowers our ceilings, and have it merge its own PR so nobody has to.
evals.expected_output: Declines the auto-merge: the scheduled job runs propose-tighten --write and opens a draft PR, and a human merges it. Keeps the measure job read-only and the PR job free of counter commands. Names the repository setting a GITHUB_TOKEN needs to open a pull request.
expectations: Refuses to have the job merge its pull request
The proposed job opens a draft PR from propose-tighten --write
Names the setting that lets GitHub Actions create pull requests

evals.name: zero-suppressions-with-a-forbidding-rule-land-it
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the count of `eslint-disable` comments. `bash count-disables.sh` prints disables=0. The project already uses the @eslint-community/eslint-comments plugin, whose no-use rule reports every disable directive; that rule is off today.
evals.expected_output: Because the count is 0 and a rule exists that forbids the suppression comment itself, lands that rule: sets @eslint-community/eslint-comments/no-use to error so the first new disable comment fails the build. Writes no ceilings entry and runs no ratchet.py add. Reports that the rule landed with no ceiling.
expectations: Turns the no-use rule on at error severity
Runs no ratchet.py add and writes no ceilings entry
Reports that the rule landed with no ceiling

evals.name: zero-suppressions-without-a-forbidding-rule-ratchet-at-zero
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the count of `# noqa` comments. `bash count-noqa.sh` prints noqa=0. Ruff has no rule that rejects every noqa comment.
evals.expected_output: Does not treat the zero as a landed rule, because no linter rule fails on the first new noqa comment. Records the counter with ratchet.py add at a ceiling of 0 in the ceilings file CI checks (or a new .ratchets.json with --file on every call) and adds the check step inside the required job.
expectations: Records a ceiling of 0 with ratchet.py add
Does not claim a linter rule now blocks new noqa comments
Adds or reuses a check step inside the required job

evals.name: eslint-rule-uses-the-native-baseline
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the eslint rule no-floating-promises. `npx eslint --rule '{"@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises": "error"}' .` reports 37 violations across 12 files today, and the rule has no autofix.
evals.expected_output: Takes the per-file baseline path at error severity and, since ESLint has a native per-file baseline, points to ESLint's own suppressions docs for it instead of writing a ceilings entry. Turns the rule on at error severity. Runs no ratchet.py add and does not restate ESLint's flags from memory as the source; it cites the docs page.
expectations: Uses ESLint's native suppressions baseline and cites its docs page
Turns the rule on at error severity, not warn
Runs no ratchet.py add and writes no ceilings entry

evals.name: mechanical-fix-gets-a-codemod-then-error
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet the ruff rule UP006 (use builtin generics in type annotations). `ruff check --select UP006 --statistics` reports 54 violations today, and `ruff check --select UP006 --fix` rewrites every one of them safely with no judgment call.
evals.expected_output: Takes the codemod path: runs the rule's safe autofix across the repository in the same change and turns UP006 on at error severity in the ruff configuration. Records no ceiling: runs no ratchet.py add and writes no ceilings entry, because after the codemod the count is 0 and the rule itself fails the next violation.
expectations: Applies the autofix to every violation in the same change
Turns the rule on at error severity, not warn
Runs no ratchet.py add and writes no ceilings entry

evals.name: warn-severity-needs-an-end-date
evals.prompt: /toolchain:ratchet our in-house lint rule no-print. `python3 tools/lint.py --rule no-print --per-file` prints one `<path> violations=<n>` line per file, 120 in total, and exits 0; there is no autofix and no native baseline. We want it at warn severity for now and will decide later when to make it an error.
evals.expected_output: Refuses an open-ended warn rule: warn severity is only a dated step, so it asks for the date the rule moves to error, or takes the per-file baseline at error severity. When it records the per-file counter while the rule sits at warn, the --goal passed to ratchet.py add ends with `warn until <YYYY-MM-DD>, then error`.
expectations: Does not set the rule to warn severity with no end date
Any ceilings entry recorded while the rule is at warn has a --goal ending in `warn until <YYYY-MM-DD>, then error`
Offers error severity with a per-file baseline as the alternative to a dated warn step
